name: Holloway & Drax Culinary Line Uniform Set
description:
Holloway & Drax supplies kitchen uniforms to the majority of GLMZ's mid-tier restaurant operations, hotel kitchens, and corporate cafeteria contracts. Their standard culinary line set includes a double-breasted chef's coat, high-waist utility trousers, and an apron — all in white with the subtle H&D chain-link logo printed at the collar. The coat fabric is a treated cotton-synthfiber blend rated for sustained heat exposure up to 200°C surface contact, with reinforced forearm panels where hot pan contact is most common. Buttons are magnetic-closure rather than traditional — faster to remove in case of spill burns, and replaceable without tools.

The set is designed with practical geneware accommodation throughout. The coat includes a rear vent panel with a hook-and-eye closure for tail clearance, and the headwear component — a structured cap rather than a traditional toque — is available in three sizes with horn-clearance cutouts on the crown, sealed with food-safe silicone edging to maintain hygienic standards. Workers with ear geneware (pointed, extended, or mobile) can substitute the cap for a certified hair-containment band at supervisor discretion. Augment compatibility is addressed through reinforced elbow patches that sit clear of standard forearm port housings. The set is washable at industrial temperatures and rated for 200 cycles before replacement is recommended — in practice, most line cooks push well past that.
cultural_context: Kitchen work in GLMZ spans a huge range — from Tier 1 communal food halls where the uniform is whatever's clean, to Tier 4 corporate dining where presentation is enforced. Holloway & Drax sits in the middle, and their white coats are ubiquitous in the city's working kitchens. The coat takes on character through stains, patches, and wear — most line cooks treat their stains as a record of service rather than something to hide.
story_hooks: A kitchen worker in a Tier 3 hotel has been wearing their Holloway & Drax coat for seven years — and the stains on it are the only record of an incident that the hotel's management wants buried.
A character needs to move through a high-security event venue undetected; the kitchen staff entrance requires a legitimate H&D uniform and a catering credential.
A batch of H&D coats from a specific supplier has been treated with a contact substance — someone is using the supply chain to reach kitchen workers specifically.

physical_description.visual_profile: A crisp white double-breasted chef's coat worn by a working-class line cook — structured yet lived-in, with the subtle H&D chain-link logo visible at the collar. The silhouette is practical and slightly boxy, designed for movement and heat protection rather than tailoring. Worn with high-waist white utility trousers and a white apron that shows honest wear.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with room for layering and movement, tapered slightly at the waist via the high-rise trousers. The coat hits mid-hip. Forearms are reinforced with visible panel sections. The structured cap sits firmly but not tight, with clear space at the crown.
physical_description.primary_material: Treated cotton-synthfiber blend rated for sustained heat exposure up to 200°C surface contact. Durable, industrial-grade, designed to withstand repeated industrial washing.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, tightly woven fabric with a slight sheen from the synthetic component. Reinforced panels have a subtly raised weave. Magnetic button closures feel smooth and satisfying. Seams are double-stitched and visible.
physical_description.color_scheme: Bright white throughout — coat, trousers, apron, and cap. The H&D chain-link logo in muted gray at the collar. Most worn examples show accumulated stains: coffee rings, grease spatters, the occasional burn mark that's been washed but not completely removed.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic buttons on the double-breasted coat front — replaceable without tools, quick to remove in case of spill burns. Hook-and-eye rear vent panel for tail clearance. Apron ties at waist and neck.
distinctive_features: Double-breasted magnetic button closure — faster removal in emergencies
Reinforced forearm panels in contrasting weave, positioned clear of standard augment ports
Rear vent panel with hook-and-eye closure for geneware tail accommodation
Structured cap with horn-clearance cutouts on crown, sealed with food-safe silicone edging
High-waist utility trousers with practical pocket depth
H&D chain-link logo printed subtly at collar — mark of a contracted kitchen worker
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional workwear — not luxury, but standard-issue in GLMZ's professional kitchen ecosystem. Signals employment in a contracted food service operation.
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of GLMZ's working-class kitchen staff — line cooks, prep cooks, kitchen runners in mid-tier restaurants, hotel kitchens, and corporate cafeterias. The H&D coat is ubiquitous enough that wearing one signals you're part of the city's food service infrastructure. Stains and wear are badges of experience, not shame.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and marked with honest wear — accumulated stains that have survived multiple industrial washes, small burn marks from pan contact, maybe a patched tear at the elbow. The cap shows creasing. The apron is noticeably worn at the ties. Most sets in active use are well past the manufacturer's 200-cycle recommendation but still serviceable.
